title: Woman Says Her Surat Househelp Has Three Flats, Including 3-BHK Worth Rs 60 Lakh: 'Tax-free Income Ki Power'  | Viral News - News18
text: What started as a casual morning chat between an employer and their house help has now turned into one of the most viral stories on X this week. A user’s post about their domestic worker buying a Rs 60-lakh 3BHK flat in Surat,while already owning multiple properties, has left netizens both stunned and curious. The post reads, “My house help came in today looking really happy. She told me she just bought a 3BHK flat in Surat worth Rs 60 lakhs, spent Rs 4 lakh on furniture and took only a Rs 10 lakh loan. I was honestly shocked. When I asked more, she mentioned that she already owns a two-floor house and a shop in the nearby Velanja village, both on rent. I just sat there speechless." Within hours, the post spread like wildfire, with hundreds of comments debating how a domestic worker managed to build such an impressive financial portfolio. While some praised her financial discipline and investment foresight, others attributed her success to India’s largely untaxed informal economy. Online Reactions: ‘The Magic of Untaxed Money’ One user quipped, “This is the magic of untaxed income — no GST, no TDS, just pure savings." Another added, “While salaried folks are stuck in EMIs and tax brackets, the cash economy quietly builds wealth." On the other hand, many defended the woman’s success story as a product of years of hard work and smart choices. “She probably saved every rupee she earned and invested in property early. That’s called planning, not privilege," a commenter wrote. The Bigger Picture: Informal Economy in Focus The viral post has reignited discussions around India’s vast informal sector — where millions of workers earn cash incomes that often go untaxed but allow greater flexibility in saving and investing. Economists note that while such earnings may seem enviable, they come without social security, pensions, or medical benefits. The internet is convinced after the post that one thing is clear – financial wisdom and ambition aren’t limited by profession or pay grade. As one user put it, “Taxed or untaxed, hustle is hustle."
